title: Losing $100 hurts more than winning $100 feels good
body: Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky found that people weigh losses more heavily than equal gains, a key part of their 1979 prospect theory. Many people turn down a coin flip that loses $100 on tails unless heads wins well over $100, often around double. Estimates of the ratio vary by study and context, and some researchers think the effect is smaller than once claimed, but it helps explain why people hate fees and cling to things they own.
